1	\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}
2	
3	We evaluated Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA) across six models, three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 instances with four-seed replication. Grounded in the Condorcet Jury Theorem, our analysis explains why SC majority voting saturates and why symbolic constraint aggregation fails to break this plateau under same-model self-extraction at the 7B--14B scale.
4	
5	The primary finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off. Fleiss' $\kappa$ generalization across aggregation methods reveals a Pareto frontier: Debate reduces $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15 (Eff-$K$: $2.0 \to 4.4$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO ($-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA); methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor ($\kappa \geq 0.40$). This trade-off constrains all same-model trace aggregation, not only symbolic approaches, and twelve remediation strategies all fail to escape it.
6	
7	The independence bottleneck quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: same-model traces produce $\kappa = 0.21$--$0.82$ (Eff-$K = 1.20$--$3.62$ at $K = 12$), meaning traces beyond 12 add negligible independent information. Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound ($+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+11.50$\,pp ProofWriter, $p < 0.001$); self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling. A directional positive trend ($+3.43$\,pp best, $+1.47$\,pp mean; none reaching $p < 0.05$) appears in one model-dataset condition, but its narrow operating range and seed sensitivity limit practical applicability. For practitioners, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost diagnostic predicting when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

We evaluated Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA) across six models, three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 instances with four-seed replication. Grounded in the Condorcet Jury Theorem, our analysis explains why SC majority voting saturates and why symbolic constraint aggregation fails to break this plateau under same-model self-extraction at the 7B--14B scale.

The primary finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off. Fleiss' $\kappa$ generalization across aggregation methods reveals a Pareto frontier: Debate reduces $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15 (Eff-$K$: $2.0 \to 4.4$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO ($-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA); methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor ($\kappa \geq 0.40$). This trade-off constrains all same-model trace aggregation, not only symbolic approaches, and twelve remediation strategies all fail to escape it.

The independence bottleneck quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: same-model traces produce $\kappa = 0.21$--$0.82$ (Eff-$K = 1.20$--$3.62$ at $K = 12$), meaning traces beyond 12 add negligible independent information. Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound ($+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+11.50$\,pp ProofWriter, $p < 0.001$); self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling. A directional positive trend ($+3.43$\,pp best, $+1.47$\,pp mean; none reaching $p < 0.05$) appears in one model-dataset condition, but its narrow operating range and seed sensitivity limit practical applicability. For practitioners, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost diagnostic predicting when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

1	\section{Analysis}
2	\label{sec:analysis}
3	
4	The regime-dependent pattern in \S\ref{sec:main-results} establishes \emph{where} SICA succeeds and fails. This section investigates \emph{why}: trace correlation quantifies the SC plateau (\S\ref{sec:effective-k}), supporting diagnostics confirm the mechanism (Appendices~\ref{app:extraction}--\ref{app:entropy}), and remediation analysis reveals a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off (\S\ref{sec:remediation}).
5	
6	\subsection{Condorcet Effective-K}
7	\label{sec:effective-k}
8	
9	Table~\ref{tab:independence} reports Fleiss' $\kappa$ and Effective-K (Eq.~\ref{eq:effk}) across 15 conditions at $K = 12$. Among instruction-tuned models, $\kappa$ ranges from 0.21 to 0.82, yielding $K_{\text{eff}} = 1.20\text{--}3.62$. Qwen3-14B in thinking mode reaches $\kappa = 0.91$ ($K_{\text{eff}} = 1.09$). The four Mistral-7B FOLIO seeds produce $\kappa \in [0.41, 0.51]$ ($K_{\text{eff}} \approx 1.8\text{--}2.2$), yet $\Delta$ ranges from $+3.43$ to $-0.49$\,pp---seed-level constraint quality, not independence, drives the variation. Two conditions are jointly necessary for positive $\Delta$: sufficient $K_{\text{eff}}$ (Qwen conditions with $K_{\text{eff}} \leq 1.30$ never improve) and sufficient SC accuracy (Mistral on ProofWriter with the highest $K_{\text{eff}} = 3.62$ but SC $= 39\%$ produces significant degradation). Even when both hold, sampling variance determines whether the constraint pool is discriminative. 41	
42	Four additional analyses confirm the mechanism underlying SICA's failure. Removing the 8.2\% non-discriminative constraints yields zero improvement. Per-domain, MAX-SAT provides a marginal edge in the intermediate-SC region (59.3\% vs.\ count-only 56.9\%) but actively hurts in the Type~C regime (36.5\% vs.\ 37.2\%), mirroring the regime-dependent pattern of SICA itself. Hyperparameter sensitivity (Appendix~\ref{app:sensitivity}): $K = 12$ is the only setting with $\Delta > 2$\,pp among five $K$ values, and only $T = 0.7$ among four temperatures yields a positive effect; both peaks coincide with relatively low SC baselines rather than reflecting hyperparameter effects per se. Entropy decomposition (Appendix~\ref{app:entropy}): all SICA effects concentrate in high-entropy problems ($\Delta$ up to $+12.8$\,pp in the intermediate-SC region), but the direction depends on the accuracy regime---high entropy signals correctable uncertainty only when the model has partial knowledge.

All nine prompt-level strategies fail. Contrastive prompting reduces non-discriminative constraints from 8.2\% to 6.0\% but newly discriminative constraints still mirror the majority ($\Delta = -1.1$\,pp). Cross-model extraction fails in both directions: weaker models extracting from stronger traces yield 0\% discriminative constraints; stronger models extracting from weaker traces produce accuracy within $\pm$1\,pp of self-extraction. Only 1 of 4 temperature settings yields a positive effect ($p = 0.092$); multi-temperature sampling produces $\Delta = 0.00$\,pp.

Independent Constraint Generation (ICG) bypasses trace-constraint coupling by generating constraints directly from premises. Despite producing objectively superior constraints---higher Z3 compilation, lower redundancy (Appendix~\ref{app:constraint-quality})---ICG yields $\Delta \approx 0$ across three seeds (McNemar $p = .206$, n.s.). 3	
4	The oracle experiments causally identify the failure source. Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.
5	
6	Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). The oracle result disambiguates: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that constraint homogenization---not voting diversity---is the proximal bottleneck.
7	
8	\paragraph{The independence-accuracy trade-off.} The $\kappa$ generalization analysis (\S\ref{sec:remediation}, Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}) constitutes the primary finding. SC, Diverse-Prompt, and ICG form a same-model ceiling at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$; Debate breaks through only at catastrophic accuracy cost (Figure~\ref{fig:kappa-accuracy}). This trade-off constrains \emph{all} same-model trace aggregation methods---not only symbolic approaches---because it arises from the model's output distribution, not from any specific aggregation procedure. Published systems that report positive results \citep{xu2026dylos, li2025aristotle, wang2025fover, pan2023logiclm} each bypass same-model self-extraction.
9	
10	\paragraph{Diagnostic tools for practitioners.} Our analysis yields two zero-cost diagnostics applicable before any constraint extraction. First, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Second, the $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: at Eff-$K \approx 2$ (typical at $K = 12$), additional traces add negligible independent information regardless of aggregation method.
11	
12	\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} The only statistically significant effects are negative: zero of nine SICA conditions reaches $p < 0.05$, while ProofWriter degradation ($p = 0.014$; $p = 0.011$) and three of six method-level conditions (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}) reach significance, all negative. Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$). This asymmetry---zero significant positives against multiple significant negatives---constitutes the strongest statistical argument for the independence bottleneck.
13	
14	\paragraph{Scale limitations and future work.} Cross-model validation shows the bottleneck worsens with scale: Qwen2.5-14B produces $\kappa = 0.74$ versus Mistral-7B's $0.44$ (Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}), narrowing the Pareto frontier rather than shifting it. Method-level interventions use Mistral-7B; whether 70B+ models reverse this trend is open. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The oracle experiments causally identify the failure source. Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.

Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). The oracle result disambiguates: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that constraint homogenization---not voting diversity---is the proximal bottleneck.

\paragraph{The independence-accuracy trade-off.} The $\kappa$ generalization analysis (\S\ref{sec:remediation}, Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}) constitutes the primary finding. SC, Diverse-Prompt, and ICG form a same-model ceiling at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$; Debate breaks through only at catastrophic accuracy cost (Figure~\ref{fig:kappa-accuracy}). This trade-off constrains \emph{all} same-model trace aggregation methods---not only symbolic approaches---because it arises from the model's output distribution, not from any specific aggregation procedure. Published systems that report positive results \citep{xu2026dylos, li2025aristotle, wang2025fover, pan2023logiclm} each bypass same-model self-extraction.

\paragraph{Diagnostic tools for practitioners.} Our analysis yields two zero-cost diagnostics applicable before any constraint extraction. First, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Second, the $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: at Eff-$K \approx 2$ (typical at $K = 12$), additional traces add negligible independent information regardless of aggregation method.

\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} The only statistically significant effects are negative: zero of nine SICA conditions reaches $p < 0.05$, while ProofWriter degradation ($p = 0.014$; $p = 0.011$) and three of six method-level conditions (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}) reach significance, all negative. Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$). This asymmetry---zero significant positives against multiple significant negatives---constitutes the strongest statistical argument for the independence bottleneck.

\paragraph{Scale limitations and future work.} Cross-model validation shows the bottleneck worsens with scale: Qwen2.5-14B produces $\kappa = 0.74$ versus Mistral-7B's $0.44$ (Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}), narrowing the Pareto frontier rather than shifting it. Method-level interventions use Mistral-7B; whether 70B+ models reverse this trend is open. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

content.content: 1	Self-Consistency (SC) majority voting over chain-of-thought traces is the dominant test-time aggregation strategy for LLMs, but accuracy gains saturate as sample count grows. The Condorcet Jury Theorem (CJT) explains this plateau: same-model traces are correlated voters, so additional samples carry diminishing independent information. Symbolic constraints in first-order logic (FOL) appear to offer a way forward, but when extracted by the same model, they inherit the traces' correlation structure. We term this the \emph{independence bottleneck}. We study it through Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA), which extracts FOL constraints from reasoning traces and selects answers via weighted partial MAX-SAT. Evaluating six models (7B--32B) across three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances and four-seed replication, we find that self-extracted constraints fail to surpass majority voting. A directional positive trend (best $+3.43$\,pp, mean $+1.47$\,pp; $p < 0.10$ in 2 of 4 seeds, none reaching $p < 0.05$) appears only in one model on one dataset at 50--55\% SC baseline. Oracle controls with gold FOL confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound, yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of the oracle ceiling. The central finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off revealed by Fleiss' $\kappa$ generalization across aggregation methods: Debate reduces inter-trace $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15, tripling the effective sample size, but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA. Methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. This trade-off constrains all same-model trace aggregation, not only symbolic approaches. The $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling, and $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost deployment diagnostic. The bottleneck is structural and scale-dependent---$\kappa$ increases from 0.44 (7B) to 0.74 (14B)---suggesting that scaling alone will not overcome it.

Evaluating six models (7B--32B) across three reasoning domains with over 3,000 instances and four-seed replication, we find that self-extracted constraints fail to surpass majority voting. A directional positive trend (best $+3.43$\,pp, mean $+1.47$\,pp; $p < 0.10$ in 2 of 4 seeds, none reaching $p < 0.05$) appears only in one model on one dataset at 50--55\% SC baseline. Oracle controls with gold FOL confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound, yet self-extraction captures only 24\% of the oracle ceiling. The central finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off revealed by Fleiss' $\kappa$ generalization across aggregation methods: Debate reduces inter-trace $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15, tripling the effective sample size, but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO and $-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA. Methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor. This trade-off constrains all same-model trace aggregation, not only symbolic approaches. The $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling, and $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost deployment diagnostic. The bottleneck is structural and scale-dependent---$\kappa$ increases from 0.44 (7B) to 0.74 (14B)---suggesting that scaling alone will not overcome it.

input.old_string: \paragraph{Independence-accuracy trade-off.} Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization} compares Fleiss' $\kappa$ across four aggregation methods on Mistral-7B FOLIO and adds Qwen2.5-14B for cross-model validation. \section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

The oracle experiments causally identify the failure source. Holding all pipeline components fixed and varying only constraint source, gold annotations yield $+14.22$\,pp on FOLIO and $+11.50$\,pp on ProofWriter ($p < 0.001$), while the best self-extraction captures only 24.1\% of this ceiling. Because the aggregation mechanism is identical in both conditions, the gap localizes entirely to extraction quality.

Trace correlation affects SICA through two channels. The \emph{direct} channel limits voting diversity: Eff-$K < 2$ for many conditions (Table~\ref{tab:independence}) confirms that same-model traces violate the CJT independence requirement, explaining the SC plateau. The \emph{indirect} channel operates through constraint quality: correlated traces produce homogeneous constraints, causing MAX-SAT to degenerate to vote counting (Appendix~\ref{app:ablation}). The oracle result disambiguates: gold constraints applied to the same correlated traces yield $+14.22$\,pp, proving that constraint homogenization---not voting diversity---is the proximal bottleneck.

\paragraph{The independence-accuracy trade-off.} The $\kappa$ generalization analysis (\S\ref{sec:remediation}, Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}) constitutes the primary finding. SC, Diverse-Prompt, and ICG form a same-model ceiling at $\kappa \approx 0.40$--$0.47$; Debate breaks through only at catastrophic accuracy cost (Figure~\ref{fig:kappa-accuracy}). This trade-off constrains \emph{all} same-model trace aggregation methods---not only symbolic approaches---because it arises from the model's output distribution, not from any specific aggregation procedure. Published systems that report positive results \citep{xu2026dylos, li2025aristotle, wang2025fover, pan2023logiclm} each bypass same-model self-extraction.

\paragraph{Diagnostic tools for practitioners.} Our analysis yields two zero-cost diagnostics applicable before any constraint extraction. First, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy predicts when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help: $C_0 < 5\%$ implies degeneration; SC $\geq 60\%$ implies confirmation bias; SC $\leq 40\%$ implies error amplification. Second, the $\kappa$-based Eff-$K$ metric quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: at Eff-$K \approx 2$ (typical at $K = 12$), additional traces add negligible independent information regardless of aggregation method.

\paragraph{Statistical evidence.} The only statistically significant effects are negative: zero of nine SICA conditions reaches $p < 0.05$, while ProofWriter degradation ($p = 0.014$; $p = 0.011$) and three of six method-level conditions (Table~\ref{tab:method_interventions}) reach significance, all negative. Oracle controls remain highly significant ($p < 0.001$). This asymmetry---zero significant positives against multiple significant negatives---constitutes the strongest statistical argument for the independence bottleneck.

\paragraph{Scale limitations and future work.} Cross-model validation shows the bottleneck worsens with scale: Qwen2.5-14B produces $\kappa = 0.74$ versus Mistral-7B's $0.44$ (Table~\ref{tab:kappa_generalization}), narrowing the Pareto frontier rather than shifting it. Method-level interventions use Mistral-7B; whether 70B+ models reverse this trend is open. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

Method-level interventions use Mistral-7B; whether 70B+ models reverse this trend is open. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

\section{Conclusion}\label{sec:conclusion}

We evaluated Symbolic Invariant Consensus Aggregation (SICA) across six models, three reasoning domains, and over 3,000 instances with four-seed replication. Grounded in the Condorcet Jury Theorem, our analysis explains why SC majority voting saturates and why symbolic constraint aggregation fails to break this plateau under same-model self-extraction at the 7B--14B scale.

The primary finding is a fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off. Fleiss' $\kappa$ generalization across aggregation methods reveals a Pareto frontier: Debate reduces $\kappa$ from 0.44 to 0.15 (Eff-$K$: $2.0 \to 4.4$) but collapses accuracy by $-18.6$\,pp on FOLIO ($-23.0$\,pp on LogiQA); methods that preserve accuracy cannot break the correlation floor ($\kappa \geq 0.40$). This trade-off constrains all same-model trace aggregation, not only symbolic approaches, and twelve remediation strategies all fail to escape it.

The independence bottleneck quantifies SC's own scaling ceiling: same-model traces produce $\kappa = 0.21$--$0.82$ (Eff-$K = 1.20$--$3.62$ at $K = 12$), meaning traces beyond 12 add negligible independent information. Oracle controls confirm the aggregation mechanism is sound ($+14.22$\,pp FOLIO, $+11.50$\,pp ProofWriter, $p < 0.001$); self-extraction captures only 24\% of this ceiling. A directional positive trend ($+3.43$\,pp best, $+1.47$\,pp mean; none reaching $p < 0.05$) appears in one model-dataset condition, but its narrow operating range and seed sensitivity limit practical applicability. For practitioners, $C_0$ combined with SC accuracy provides a zero-cost diagnostic predicting when symbolic augmentation is unlikely to help. Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, and multi-model pipelines.

Table~\ref{tab:cross_model_kappa} compares trace independence across Mistral-7B and Qwen2.5-14B on the same benchmarks. On FOLIO ($n = 204$), Qwen2.5-14B produces substantially higher inter-trace correlation ($\kappa = 0.74$, $K_{\text{eff}} = 1.32$) than Mistral-7B ($\kappa = 0.44$, $K_{\text{eff}} = 2.02$): the stronger model's traces agree more, leaving less room for any aggregation method to extract independent signal. ProofWriter shows a similar pattern ($\kappa = 0.62$ vs.\ $0.21$), though Mistral-7B's low $\kappa$ on ProofWriter reflects low accuracy (SC $= 39\%$) rather than genuine diversity. The monotonic relationship between model capability and $\kappa$ suggests that the independence bottleneck is not a limitation of weak models but a structural consequence of capable models producing consistent outputs.

## D070/D074 Update: Method-Level Interventions Also Fail — "Fundamental Limitation" Confirmed

### Three Method Lines × Two Datasets = All Negative (D074)

D070 从纯 analysis 升级为 analysis + method paper，但三条方法线全面失败（D074 确认），反而强化了原始 analysis 结论。

**方法×数据集完整结果**：
| Method | FOLIO-204 | LogiQA-200 | Failure Mode |
|--------|-----------|------------|--------------|
| ICG (Independent Constraint Gen.) | Δ=-2.0pp (3-seed: -2.0/+1.5/-1.0, mean=-0.5pp±1.8pp, 噪声) | Δ=-0.5pp | Neutral — 独立约束质量≈trace-sourced约束 |
| Contrastive (Pro/Con Scoring) | Δ≈-16pp | Δ≈-7pp (interim) | Harmful — 26% degenerate scoring, pro/con 不平衡 |
| Debate (Proposer/Critic) | Δ=-18.6pp | Δ≈-28pp (interim) | Catastrophic — 7B 模型角色扮演严重退化推理 |

**三种失败模式的分析价值**（论文 "Why Methods Fail" section）：
1. **ICG (neutral)**: 独立于 traces 生成的约束不比 trace-sourced 约束更好。说明 bottleneck 不仅是 "约束来自 traces"，而是模型的推理偏差从问题理解阶段就存在——独立约束和 trace-sourced 约束继承相同的 model bias。
2. **Contrastive (harmful)**: 强制 pro/con 评估引入 degenerate scoring（26% 问题无法有效区分）。7B 模型无法可靠生成平衡的对立约束——pro 约束系统性多于 con（94 pro vs 65 con），confirmation bias 从约束提取转移到了约束生成。
3. **Debate (catastrophic)**: Proposer/Critic/Defense 多角色链在 7B 模型上导致答案质量严重退化。辩论不仅未增加多样性，反而引入了角色扮演的额外认知负担。同模型辩论 = 同源性 + 角色扮演退化，双重损失。

**Scale limitation caveat**: 所有方法测试在 7B 模型上。7B 模型生成 Z3 格式 FOL 约束的能力不足（ICG 多题 "0/N constraints parsed"）。14B+ 模型可能有不同结果——这既是 limitation 也是 future work 入口。

### κ Generalization — Independence-Accuracy Trade-off (D075, CAPSTONE FINDING)

exp-077 测量三种聚合方式在 Mistral-7B FOLIO-204 上的 κ 和 Eff-K：
| 聚合方式 | Fleiss' κ | Eff-K | 名义 K |
|----------|----------|-------|--------|
| Self-Consistency | 0.4384 | 2.02 | 10 |
| Diverse-Prompt | 0.4030 | 2.21 | 12 |
| LLM-Debate | 0.1549 | 4.44 | 12 |

结合 exp-076 Debate Δ=-18.6pp 的准确率数据，揭示**同模型框架下的 fundamental independence-accuracy trade-off**：
- **SC/Diverse-Prompt**: κ~0.4，traces 高度相关但准确率正常。换 prompt 策略不改善独立性（Δκ=0.04）。
- **Debate**: κ=0.15，成功打破 trace 相关性（Eff-K 从 2.0 跃升到 4.4），但准确率崩溃 -18.6pp。低 κ 不代表"更独立的推理"——是 disagreement amplification（系统性噪声）。
- **Trade-off 本质**: 同一模型的推理能力是固定的。要么输出一致（高 κ, 正确但不独立），要么输出分歧（低 κ, 独立但不正确）。Condorcet Jury Theorem 要求 both independent AND accurate，同模型框架下无法同时满足。

**论文叙事升级**: 从 "methods fail" → "independence-accuracy trade-off is fundamental to same-model reasoning"。突破瓶颈需要跨模型方案（不同模型天然更独立），Oracle 实验（gold FOL 来自外部知识源）已间接验证了这一点。

### New Claim 6 (D070/D074)

6. **Method-Level Interventions Cannot Break the Bottleneck**: 三种针对 independence bottleneck 不同环节的方法（ICG→循环依赖, Contrastive→confirmation bias, Debate→trace 同质性）在 2 个数据集上全部失败。加上之前 9 种 prompt-level 修复，共 12 种修复尝试全败。这证明 independence bottleneck 不是单一环节的问题，而是 same-model self-extraction 的根本性限制。

### New Claim 7: Symbolic Confirmation Bias (D082 — CORE FINDING)

7. **Symbolic Confirmation Bias**: LLM 从 CoT traces 提取的 FOL 约束系统性确认 trace 自身（可能错误的）答案，而非独立验证 ground truth。
   - SICA 判对题：gold constraint 78.1%，bias ratio = 0.28
   - SICA 判错题：错误 constraint 83.3%，bias ratio = **4.97×**
   - 97.6% SICA 错误与 SC 错误完全重合
   - SICA 翻盘的 12 例来自 minority trace diversity（43% gold support），不是 symbolic reasoning
   - **因果链**：模型推理→答案→从含答案 trace 提取 FOL→约束确认答案→聚合≈SC
   - **CEGIS 验证**：迭代精炼 R1 +3.43pp < 原始 SICA +4.9pp → 约束一致性不是瓶颈，偏向性才是
   - **Quality Ladder 验证**：L1 ≈ L0 << L3 → bottleneck 在 traces（同源输入），不在 extractor

### New Claim 8: Process-κ (D082 — NEW METRIC)

8. **Process-Level Independence (Process-κ)**: answer-κ 低估真实独立性瓶颈。CoT 推理过程相似性远高于答案一致性。
   - Mistral-7B FOLIO-204：CoT cosine similarity **0.69** >> answer-κ **0.41**
   - 两者几乎无相关性：r = -0.06, p = 0.36
   - 仅 **9.3%** trace 对是"殊途同归"（同答案不同路径）
   - answer-κ 是 true independence bottleneck 的 lower bound
   - 适用于所有 LLM trace aggregation 方法，不限于 SICA

- **Problem**: LLMs' reasoning can be improved by sampling multiple chains-of-thought and aggregating via majority voting (self-consistency). - **Theoretical lens**: Condorcet Jury Theorem requires voter independence. We quantify trace independence via Fleiss' κ and show Effective-K << nominal K. This explains the fundamental limitation of same-model trace aggregation.
- **Systematic evaluation**: SICA (MAX-SAT over FOL constraints) across 3 domains × 5 model families. Oracle control separates extraction vs aggregation failure. - **Regime characterization**: Three failure modes (Type A/B/C) + narrow Goldilocks zone. C0+SC as deployment diagnostic.

      - "Independence-accuracy trade-off (exp-077): Debate breaks κ (0.44→0.15) but collapses accuracy (-18.6pp). Diverse-Prompt ≈ SC κ. Same-model methods face a fundamental Pareto frontier."
      - "This trade-off explains WHY same-model methods must fail, not just that they do. Breaking correlation within a single model's distribution necessarily degrades the signal."
      - "Published methods (DyLoS, Aristotle, FoVer, Logic-LM) bypass same-model extraction — consistent with trade-off: cross-model/external sources are naturally independent without sacrificing quality"
      - "Statistical evidence: 0/4 seeds significant positive; only significant effects are negative"
      - "C0+SC deployment diagnostic: C0<5%→degenerate, high SC→confirmation bias, low SC→error amplification"
      - "Three paths forward trade simplicity for independence: trained extractors, external provers, multi-model pipelines — all introduce signal outside the model's own distribution"
    dependencies: [experiments, analysis]

  - section: conclusion
    file: conclusion.tex
    word_budget: 300
    core_bullets:
      - "SICA evaluated: 6 models spanning 3 families, 3 reasoning domains, N>3,000, 4-seed replication"
      - "Independence bottleneck: κ=0.21–0.82, Eff-K=1.20–3.62 → explains SC plateau and SICA failure"
      - "Intermediate-SC region: +3.43pp best seed (ns), 4-seed mean +1.47pp (2/4 positive, 2/4 null/negative)"
      - "Oracle +14.22pp/+11.50pp (p<0.001); 12 remediations all fail; independence-accuracy trade-off explains why"
      - "Limitations: trained extractors untested, narrow intermediate-SC zone, 7B-scale method testing, formal reasoning domains only"
    dependencies: [experiments, analysis]

    description: >

      dedup → weighted partial MAX-SAT (Z3) → answer selection.
      Oracle branch replaces self-extracted constraints with gold FOL.
      Independence bottleneck annotation at extraction stage.
    narrative_intent: >
      The pipeline looks like it should introduce independent symbolic
      signal, but self-extraction inherits the same trace correlation —
      the independence bottleneck manifests at the extraction stage.
    design_notes:
      - "Existing figure in paper; update to annotate independence bottleneck clearly"
      - "Add oracle branch as parallel path with green highlight"
      - "Add method-level intervention points (ICG/Contrastive/Debate) as annotation"
    placement: method
    aspect_ratio: "16:6"
    data_source: "manual (diagram)"
    status: "EXISTS — label update needed"

  - fig_id: fig2_regime_scatter

    description: >
      SC accuracy (x-axis) vs SICA Δpp (y-axis) scatter plot.

      as separate points. Color/marker by model family.

    narrative_intent: >

      setting with Δ>2pp, T=0.7 is an isolated spike. Both peaks

    design_notes:
